name: rows_sum_to_one
why: No probability mass is lost or created, including at the cap.

name: cap_clipping_mass
why: Arrivals that overflow the cap are clipped onto state 200 with the right probability.

name: dispatch_transitions
why: Dispatching with s<K (even s=0) ships everyone; s>K leaves s-K behind.

name: cost_table
why: Costs follow the stated convention; dispatching an empty station still costs cf.

name: horizon_T1
why: T=1: V0(s) = min(hold cost, dispatch cost). Catches an off-by-one in the backward loop.

name: horizon_T2
why: T=2 recursion matches an independent loop implementation (no matrices).

name: horizon_array_shape
measured: V shape (501, 201), V[T] all zero = True
why: Exactly T=500 backups: V[T]=0 terminal and V[0] is time zero.

name: bruteforce_enumeration_T12
measured: max |enumerated optimum - backward induction| = 1.14e-13 over 7 start states x 4096 sequences
why: Backward induction equals literal enumeration of all 2^12 action sequences (deterministic arrivals A=3).

name: T500_vs_infinite_horizon
why: Finite-horizon T=500 and infinite-horizon solutions agree, since gamma^500 ~ 7e-12.

name: VI_equals_PI
why: Two independent algorithms reach the same fixed point.

name: PI_start_independence
measured: always_hold: 6 iters, dV=0.0e+00, same policy=True; always_dispatch: 5 iters, dV=0.0e+00, same policy=True; random: 4 iters, dV=0.0e+00, same policy=True
expected: same V and policy from all starts
why: Policy iteration converges to the optimum from any initial policy.

name: PI_monotone_improvement
measured: max_s (V_{k+1} - V_k) over all iterations = 0.00e+00; iterations = 6
why: Policy improvement theorem holds numerically; also catches sign errors in cost vs reward.

name: PI_few_iterations
why: Policy iteration is Newton-like and should need few iterations; many would suggest a bug.

name: PI_eval_solve_vs_sweeps
why: The linear-solve policy evaluation agrees with brute-force iterative evaluation.

name: VI_contraction_bound
why: Value iteration error stays under the theoretical contraction bound at every iteration.

name: VI_residual_ratio_to_gamma
why: Asymptotic VI rate equals gamma because the constant direction (average cost > 0) contracts exactly at gamma.

name: VI_stopping_rule
why: The stopping tolerance eps(1-gamma)/gamma delivers the promised accuracy.

name: VI_iteration_count
why: Iteration count consistent with the contraction rate.

name: V_monotone_and_slope_bound
why: An extra waiting customer cannot help and costs at most ch every period forever.

name: threshold_structure
why: Optimal policy is of control-limit type (no 'hold' above the first dispatch state).

name: threshold_value
why: Dispatching roughly when the shuttle can be filled.

name: V_convexity_observation
expected: >= 0 (not guaranteed: min over actions of convex functions need not be convex)
why: Observation only.

name: cost_scaling_x10
measured: relative max |V' - 10 V| = 2.86e-16, same policy = True
why: Scaling both costs by 10 scales V by exactly 10 and leaves the policy unchanged (no hard-coded constants).

name: limit_ch_zero
why: With no holding cost there is no reason to ever pay cf.

name: limit_cf_zero
measured: dispatch at all s>=1: True (s=0 is a tie -> hold)
why: With free dispatch, always ship.

name: limit_gamma_zero
why: A myopic agent never dispatches under these parameters.

name: threshold_vs_gamma
expected: nonincreasing in gamma; dispatch first appears around gamma ~ 0.7-0.8
why: More patient agents dispatch earlier; dispatch first used at gamma = 0.75.

name: cap_300_vs_200
measured: max |V_300 - V_200| on s<=200 = 4.55e-13; policy identical = True
why: The optimal policy never lets the queue approach 200, so the cap is irrelevant.

name: cap_400_vs_200
measured: max |V_400 - V_200| on s<=200 = 4.55e-13; policy identical = True
why: The optimal policy never lets the queue approach 200, so the cap is irrelevant.

name: cap_30_vs_200
why: Even a cap of 30 gives identical values on the shared states.

name: cap_10_artifact
expected: V lower and never dispatch: overflow customers vanish for free, so a tiny cap is an artifact
why: Shows what the cap assumption does when it is binding.

name: cost_timing_sensitivity
measured: threshold with holding charged on leftover = 13; on post-arrival queue = 13; V(0): 576.67 vs 696.67
why: Charging ch on the post-arrival queue adds the constant ch*E[A] = 6 per period, i.e. exactly 120 to every V (until the cap binds), so the policy cannot change: the timing ambiguity is provably harmless here.

name: monte_carlo_V0
why: Simulating the optimal policy with random arrivals reproduces V*(0) (independent of the matrices).

name: optimal_beats_alternatives
why: The optimum is no worse than trivial policies.

name: deterministic_arrivals_forward_sim
why: With A=3 every period, plain-loop simulation of the DP policy matches DP exactly.

name: stationary_identity
measured: (1-gamma) E_mu[V*] = 32.344188; average cost g = 32.344188; stationarity residual 6.1e-14
why: Exact identity linking discounted values and the long-run average cost under the optimal policy.

name: dispatch_frequency
measured: threshold 13 < K=15 so dispatches ship fewer than 15; frequency = 0.2133 (> 0.2), mean customers served per dispatch = 14.06
why: Flow balance with partial loads: frequency x mean load = mean arrival rate (3).

name: average_cost_prediction
why: Back-of-envelope: dispatch about every 5 periods (20/period) plus holding (about 2 x queue).
